scenario.name: cipn_28d
scenario.notes: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (paclitaxel-type). Mechanistically distinct from traumatic models: NO mechanical nerve lesion; axonal mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress are the primary drivers, with TLR4-dependent glial activation. Seeds emphasize the axonal-mitotoxic axis (mitochondrial dysfunction, ROS) plus TLR4/TNF/IL-6 neuroinflammation; BDNF and MMP-9 seeded lower than SNI/CCI reflecting their secondary role. Sustained drives model a fractional dosing schedule: tonic ROS/mitochondrial/ TNF elevation during the treatment window only (ticks 0-11), so the post-treatment trajectory probes partial reversibility versus persistence, the clinically decisive question for CIPN.
